The Oriental Insurance Company ... vs Rosannagari Veera
Obanna, on 5 May, 2023
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Mallikarjuna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A. No.3121 Of 2014
Judgment :
1. Aggrieved by the order dated 31.10.2012 in M.V.O.P. No.582 of 2011 passed by the Chairman,

entities.text:
Oriental Insurance Company ... vs Rosannagari Veera
Obanna

sentences.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal- cum - Iv Additional District Judge (F.T.C.), Anantapur (for short
'the Tr
ibunal')
, the 2nd respondent preferred this appeal questioning the order passed by the Tribunal in fastening the liability on it to pay the awarded compensation.
2. For convenience, the parties will be referred to as arrayed in the claim petition.

3. The claimants filed a petition under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act for compensation of Rs.6,00,000/- for the death of Boya Rosannagari Obulesu (hereinafter referred to as 'the deceased')
in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 05.07.2011.
Petitioners 1 and 2 are the parents, and the third petitioner is the deceased's brother.
4. The claimant's case is that on 05.07.2011 at about 7.00 PM, the deceased, along with other coolie workers, left Thoundur for Narpala Village.

After crossing Parnapalli and Dadithota at approximately 08.30 PM, the Bolero Goods Van bearing No.AP-02- X-8729 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle') reached Eswaramanyam of Tadimarri limits; the offending vehicle's driver /2/
drove it rashly and negligently, then the offending vehicle turned turtle; the deceased fell and sustained severe bleeding injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Government General Hospital,
Anantapur, where the doctor declared him dead.
A case was registered in Crime No.19 of 2011 of Tadimarri Police Station for the offence under Sections 337, 338 and 304-A of I.P.C. against the offending vehicle's driver.
5. The 1st respondent remained exparte.

6. The 2nd respondent filed a counter, contending that the deceased was an unauthorized passenger in the offending vehicle; the 1st respondent violated the terms of the policy by carrying eight persons even though the seating capacity in the van is only three.
As such, the 2nd respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
7. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal formulated the necessary issues for consideration.
Before the Tribunal, on behalf of petitioners, PWs.1 and 2 got examined and marked Exs.A1 to A5.

On behalf of the 2ndrespondent, RW.1 got examined and marked Ex.B1.
8.
Appreciating evidence on record, the Tribunal finds that the deceased is not an unauthorized passenger.
The Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.4,22,000/- with interest at 7.5% p.a., against respondents from the petition date.
The petition against the 3rd petitioner is dismissed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company vehemently contended that the deceased was an unauthorized passenger in the offending vehicle; the 1st respondent violated the terms and conditions of the policy by carrying eight persons even though the seating capacity of the said goods van is only three.
The driver of the offending vehicle has no valid driving license at the time of the accident.
The interest awarded by the Tribunal is against the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court.
10. Learned counsel for the respondents 1 to 3/ claimants supported the findings and observations of the learned Tribunal.
11. Now point for determination is 1.
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?
2. Whether the Tribunal erred in fastening the liability on the insurance company to pay the compensation?

12. After reading the material on record and the submissions made on behalf of both sides and perusal of the order passed by the Tribunal, this Court views no dispute regarding the death of the deceased due to injuries in the accident.
The Tribunal's finding that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle's driver is not disputed.

In the grounds of appeal also, the insurance company contends that only because the offending vehicle's driver drove the vehicle rashly and /4/ negligently at high speed the offending vehicle turned turtle.
It is not in dispute that the deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.
The Tribunal's finding that the deceased being a cleaner of the offending vehicle, travelled in it at the time of the accident is not questioned in this appeal.
The relationship claimed in the petition that petitioners 1 and 2 are the parents of the deceased and petitioner.
No.3 is the deceased's brother is not disputed.

Point No.1 :
a.
The evidence on record shows that the deceased was the cleaner of the offending vehicle at the time of the accident.
The Tribunal observed that the petitioners failed to establish that the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/-, but it assessed the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/-.
The Tribunal's findings that the deceased was a bachelor and aged about 22 years as of the date of the accident are not disputed.
The Tribunal applied the multiplier of '14' by considering the deceased's mother's age.
b. In the motor accident claims, if the deceased is a bachelor, as laid down by the Apex Court in a catena of judgments, to assess the loss of earnings, a bachelor's age should be considered.

sentences.text:
Recently, a three-Judge bench of the Apex Court, in Royal /5/ Sundaram Alliance Vs Mandala Yadagari Goud1 by referring to the principles laid down in Sube Singh Vs.
Shyam Singh2 and Reshma Kumari Vs. Madan Mohan3, it was categorically taken that the age of the deceased and not the age of the parents would be the factor to take the multiplier to be applied.

entities.text: Royal /5/ Sundaram Alliance Vs Mandala Yadagari Goud1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant portion of the Judgment, in paragraphs 11 to 13, is extracted hereunder:

"11.....the loss of dependency is thus stated to be based on: (i) additions/ deductions to be made for arriving at the income; (ii) the deductions to be made towards personal and living expenses of the deceased; and (iii) the multiplier to be applied concerning the age of the deceased.
It is the third aspect of significance, and Reshma Kumari (supra) categorically states that it does not want to re-visit the law settled in Sarla Verma on this behalf.

12....the Constitution Bench in National Insurance Company Ltd., V. Pranay Sethi 2017 ACJ 2700 (S.C.) has also been referred to in Sube Singh v. Shyam Singh 2018 ACJ 737 (S.C.).
13..... There is no need to take up this issue settled by the judgments mentioned above of the three- Judge Bench and also relying upon the Constitution Bench that it is the age of the deceased which has to be taken into account and not the age of the dependents."
c.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., V. Pranay Sethi 2017 ACJ 2700 (S.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sube Singh v. Shyam Singh 2018 ACJ 737 (S.C.)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By following the principles laid down by the Apex Court in Royal Sundaram's case (supra1), Sube Singh's case (supra2), and Reshma Kumari's case (supra3), this Court views that the 2019 ACJ 1644 2018 ACJ 737 (S.C.) 2013 ACJ 1253 (S.C.) /6/ Tribunal wrongly took the age of the deceased's mother in determining the loss of earnings of the deceased.

d. To assess the loss of earnings, this Court relied on the Judgment of the Apex Court in Sarala Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation4 in which the Apex Court provided the table of the multiplier to be considered for the claims made under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

entities.text: Sarala Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the multiplier for the persons aged between 21 and 25 is provided as '18'.

After deducting half of the annual earnings towards the personal expenses of the deceased, the yearly loss of earnings arrived at Rs.18,000/-, and thereby the loss of dependency would come at Rs.3,24,000/-(18,000 x 18). e.

In a case between National Insurance Company Ltd., V.Pranay Sethi 5 the Apex Court awarded a total sum of Rs.70,000/- under conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral expenses.
It was further held that the sum should be enhanced at 10% every three years.

It was held thus in Paragraph 61:
"(viii) Reasonable figures under conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs.15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Res.15,000/- respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years."

In Magma General Ins. Co. Ltd., v. Nanu Ram6, at paragraph 8, the Apex Court held that:

sentences.text: " (8.6)...the Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial and welfare legislation.
The Court is duty-bound and entitled to award 'just compensation, irrespective of whether any plea on that behalf was raised by the claimant.
(8.7) A Constitution Bench of this Court in Pranay Sethi, 2017 ACJ 2700 (S.C.), dealt with the various heads under which compensation is to be awarded in a death case.
One of these heads is the loss of consortium.
In legal parlance, 'consortium' is a compendious term which encompasses 'spousal consortium', parental consortium', and filial consortium.

The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance,
solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to his family.
Concerning a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse (Rajesh v. Rajbir Singh 2013 ACJ 1403 (S.C.).
The parental consortium is granted to the child upon the premature death of a parent, for loss of 'parental aid, protection, affection, society, discipline, guidance and training.
The filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensate in the case of the accidental death of a child.
An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose their child during their lifetime.

Children are valued for their love,
affection, companionship and their role in the family unit."
g.
The Judgment in Pranay Sethi's case (Supra5) was rendered in the year 2017.
Therefore, the claimants are entitled to a 10% 2018 ACJ 2782 /8/ enhancement of conventional heads.

In all, the claimants are entitled to the compensation as detailed below:
Towards loss of dependency Rs.3,24,000/-
 Towards funeral expenses Rs. 16,500/-
 Towards loss of estate Rs. 16,500/-
Towards filial consortium Rs. 65,000/-
In view of the above, this Court views that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.
Accordingly, point No.1 is answered.

Point No.2 :

sentences.text: Though the appellant/insurance company contends that the 1 st respondent/owner of the offending vehicle violated the policy terms and conditions, no evidence is placed.
In the absence of such evidence, the Tribunal is not expected to give a finding favourable to the insurance company.

The respondent/insurance company has placed an Ex.B1-insurance policy, which shows that the insurance company collected an amount of Rs.50/- towards Addl.
L.L. - Paid Driver, Conductor, Cleaner, I.M.T. 40.
As such, the contention raised by the insurance company that it had not collected any premium to cover the risk of the cleaner cannot be accepted.
b. Even otherwise, in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited, rep.
By its Branch Manager Kadapa v. Pujala Chenchu /9/ Nagaiah and others7 Common High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad held that.

entities.text: Manager Kadapa v. Pujala Chenchu /9/ Nagaiah and others7
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Common High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: "the contention of the appellant that it is not under obligation to cover the liability arising out of the death or bodily injuries to a cleaner unless an extra premium is paid cannot be accepted.
The vehicle was admittedly a goods carriage, and a cleaner engaged in such vehicle is covered by clause (i)(c) of proviso Section 147(1) of the M.V.Act.
Therefore, we can take no exception to the order passed by the Commissioner, holding that the 3rd respondent and the appellant herein are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

c. In the case Mandava Lakshminarayana and another v.
K.V.S.S.Mallikarjuna Rao and another 8 Common High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad held that "as regards the second aspect, it is a matter of common knowledge that in the heavy transport vehicles, invariably cleaners are appointed.

entities.text:
Mandava Lakshminarayana and another v.
K.V.S.S.Mallikarjuna Rao and another 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Common High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: At least in the case of goods vehicles, once goods are loaded, the driver can drive a vehicle without the assistance of anyone.
In the case of heavy transport vehicles, the cleaner must take every precaution, including proper upkeep of the vehicle.

For practical purposes, he acts as a caretaker of the vehicle, both when the vehicle is in motion and parked."
d.

Mere perusal of section 147 thereof would have made to know that the taking out of a policy to cover the risk of the persons employed on motor vehicles is mandatory,
and the minimum coverage should be to the extent it is provided for under the Workmen's Compensation Act (for short 'the W.C.Act') 7 2011 (2) A.L.T., 357 8 2014 ACJ 1739 /10/ e.
The case of the petitioners is that the offending vehicle is a goods van.
The respondents have not disputed the same.

f. By following the observations made in the above decisions, this Court is of the view that as the vehicle was a goods carriage and a cleaner engaged in such a vehicle is covered by clause (i)(c) of proviso 2, section 147(1) of MV Act.
Accordingly, point No.2 is answered.

sentences.text: Given the discussion above, I do not find any substance in the appeal, and I do not find any reason to interfere with the impugned order in the present appeal.
14. Accordingly, the appeal being devoid of merits, is hereby dismissed without costs, and the order dt.31.10.2012 passed by the Tribunal in MVOP.No.582 of 2011 is hereby confirmed.
15. Miscellaneous Petitions, if any, pending in this appeal shall stand closed.
_ JUSTICE T.MALLIKARJUNA RAO Date :05.05.2023.
